mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows, and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for GDP growth vs. returns falls below 0.05 over any 2-year window, or 20-day returns in expanding economies are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6.0% triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as improved labor market conditions boost corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of UNRATE < 6.0% are not significantly higher than average (t-test p > 0.05) or UNRATE remains above 6.0% despite positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% alongside a quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1), the combined effect of monetary tightening and demand growth compresses discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not rise significantly when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and GDPC1 > 15,000 (t-test p > 0.05) or the proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, high supply growth (INDPRO > 105) combined with elevated CPIAUCSL (CPI inflation) signals market overvaluation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite high INDPRO and CPIAUCSL values (t-test p > 0.05) or the combination does not occur in the data.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, the conflicting signals of tightening monetary policy and improving labor markets create uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not decline when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in supply (INDPRO) above 105 indicates robust production capacity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market optimism grows.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns fail to rise significantly when INDPRO is increasing (t-test p > 0.05) or the trend reverses.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in labor employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 140,000 workers triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals strong labor demand and corporate growth prospects.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not rise when PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 (t-test p > 0.05) or the employment rate plateaus.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery phase, a surge in demand (RSAFS > 425,881) alongside falling unemployment (UNRATE < 7.3) creates momentum for positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market confidence rebuilds.
failure_condition: 60-day returns fail to rise significantly when RSAFS > 425,881 and UNRATE < 7.3 (t-test p > 0.05) or the proxies move in opposite directions.
